jobs.title: AI Principal Architect
jobs.description: Our Purpose Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. Title and Summary AI Principal Architect Mastercard's Business & Market Insights (B&MI) group empowers organizations to achieve growth and innovation goals by delivering unparalleled data-driven intelligence and cutting-edge AI solutions. By harnessing proprietary data, frontier generative AI, and global expertise, B&MI helps businesses make smarter, faster, and more impactful decisions. We transform complex, multi-modal data into agentic systems and generative applications that drive measurable business outcomes and sustained competitive advantage. We're looking for a Principal Architect, Generative AI & ML Engineering, for the Operational Intelligence Program within B&MI. As a principal-level technical leader, you'll define the architecture vision and technical strategy for our agentic AI platform. On this platform, agents make extensive tool calls into enterprise services and APIs and must run securely, reliably, and at scale. You'll set the standards teams build on across tool calling, multi-agent orchestration, self-correcting agents, memory, retrieval, and LLMOps. You'll also make the key decisions on models, platforms, and trade-offs. Working closely with engineering, product, security, and business leaders, you'll shape the long-term direction of Gen AI across B&MI and mentor architects and senior engineers. You'll also stay hands-on with prototypes that de-risk big bets. The hardest problems in enterprise Gen AI are reliability, integration, security, and scale. If you've solved them as a backend or distributed systems architect and have started applying that experience to LLM systems, we'd love to hear from you. Roles & Responsibilities • Own the architecture and technical roadmap for the Operational Intelligence Gen AI platform, defining reference architectures and standards that teams across the program can reuse and scale. • Architect the enterprise tool-calling layer, setting standards for how internal services, data platforms, and external APIs are exposed to agents as tools. This covers schemas, contracts, versioning, access control, and resilient execution (parallel and chained calls, retries, timeouts, idempotency, circuit breakers, and fallbacks). • Set the architecture for multi-agent and skills-based agent systems (e.g., LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen), including when to use agents versus deterministic workflows and how agents coordinate, delegate, and share context. • Design self-correcting agent patterns: tool critics and verifiers that check tool selection, arguments, and results, plus reflection and plan-and-execute loops that catch errors before agents act or respond. • Architect agent memory and state for long-running, multi-step sessions, including short- and long-term memory (e.g., Mem0, Zep, LangGraph memory), session persistence, and memory scoping and retention. • Define retrieval architecture for grounded reasoning, including Self-RAG, Corrective RAG (CRAG), adaptive retrieval, and Graph-RAG, built on vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, pgvector, OpenSearch) and knowledge graphs (e.g., Neo4j, AWS Neptune). • Design the inference and orchestration layer for high throughput, covering async processing, streaming, caching, rate limiting, and model routing across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and open-source models. • Establish the LLMOps architecture on Databricks (AWS), including MLflow, CI/CD for prompts and agents, and model lineage. Set platform-wide evaluation and observability standards: end-to-end tracing of tool calls, tool-selection accuracy, task success rates, cost, and latency. • Build security and Responsible AI into the architecture, including guardrails, prompt-injection defenses, hallucination mitigation, data privacy, and audit trails that meet Mastercard's data ethics and regulatory standards. • Own key architecture decisions and trade-offs, such as build versus buy, model and vendor selection, and cost versus latency versus accuracy, documented through architecture decision records. Assess emerging models, frameworks, and standards such as MCP for production readiness. • Lead design reviews and partner with engineering, product, security, and data teams to align on architecture and raise the engineering bar across the program. • Stay hands-on, building prototypes and reference implementations that de-risk decisions and give teams a working starting point. All About You • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, AI/ML, or Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. • Significant experience architecting large-scale distributed systems in production, including microservices, event-driven systems, data platforms, and cloud-native infrastructure. • Deep expertise in API design and systems integration, including contracts, security models, and reliability patterns for services consumed by many teams. You understand what changes when the consumer is an LLM. • Hands-on experience designing and shipping LLM-powered systems in production, especially agents that use tool/function calling, memory, and retrieval, and a clear view of how they fail. • Strong Python skills for hands-on prototyping (async programming, FastAPI or similar), plus SQL proficiency. • Deep experience with at least one major cloud platform (AWS preferred; Azure or GCP welcome), including its AI services such as Bedrock, SageMaker, Azure OpenAI, or Vertex AI. • A solid grounding in security, privacy, and compliance for enterprise systems, ideally in financial services or another regulated industry. • The ability to influence without authority, aligning engineering, product, and leadership around a technical direction and explaining trade-offs in business terms. • Nice to have: hands-on experience with tool critics, Self-RAG, CRAG, reflection loops, memory frameworks such as Mem0 or Zep, MCP tool servers, or agent evaluation frameworks. • Nice to have: exposure to fine-tuning (LoRA, PEFT, RLHF), multimodal models, or knowledge graphs. • Coming from backend or distributed systems architecture? The hardest problems in enterprise Gen AI are reliability, integration, security, and scale, and you've solved them before. If you've started applying that experience to LLM systems, we want to hear from you, even if you haven't used every tool listed here. Corporate Security Responsibility All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must: Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices; Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed; Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

jobs.title: Software Dev Engineer
jobs.description: DESCRIPTION Amazon Customer Service (CS) is hiring a Software Development Engineer II to join the Associate Experience team. Our organization is at the forefront of customer experience — seeking to delight our customers in every interaction they have, whether through self-serve technology and tools (e.g., chatbots), or by interacting directly with our Customer Service Associates (CSA). Customer Service works to offer effective, empathetic, and efficient issue resolution when our customers need us, and we are also champions of driving defects out of customer experiences across the entire company, relentlessly advocating on behalf of customers and keeping them at the heart of everything we do. As a Software Development Engineer II on this team, you will design, develop, and own comprehensive customer engagement services and solutions that anticipate and resolve customer questions at global scale. You will partner with cross-functional teams to drive technical strategy and improvements to our technology platform, owning systems that power the ultimate customer service experience. You will also contribute to engineering best practices and mentor junior engineers on the team. You should be somebody who thrives on solving difficult technical problems, designing scalable solutions, and feels strongly about building reliable software with a customer-centric mindset. We use Scrum, test-driven development, and continuous deployment to deliver projects by making effective trade-offs between time, quality, and resources. If you are results-oriented, data-driven, and passionate about creating innovative customer experiences through technology, we would love to connect with you. Key job responsibilities Design, develop, and own software services and tools that solve difficult business and operational problems, delivering with a focus on simplicity and scalability Optimize and enhance existing systems for performance, reliability, and maintainability at Amazon scale Make informed technical decisions on system design, technology selection, and problem-solving approaches with limited guidance Identify and mitigate technical risks early in the development lifecycle, escalating when appropriate Partner with engineers and cross-functional teams to contribute to design reviews, align on technical direction, and drive improvements across team boundaries Make effective trade-offs between time, quality, and resources to deliver high-quality results within project timelines Track, analyze, and act on key metrics to optimize system performance and drive continuous improvement Identify and implement engineering process improvements, contributing to operational excellence and best practices across the team Mentor junior engineers by providing technical guidance, conducting code reviews, and fostering a culture of learning and high standards Write clear technical documentation, including design documents and operational runbooks, to support system ownership and team knowledge sharing A day in the life As a Software Development Engineer II on the Associate Experience team, no two days look exactly the same — but each one centers on building technology that makes a real difference for Customer Service Associates (CSAs) and the customers they serve. You might start your morning reviewing metrics from a recent deployment, analyzing how a feature you own is performing at scale and identifying areas for optimization. Then you could be deep in a design review with your team, debating trade-offs between approaches for a new generative AI-powered automation feature. After that, you shift to hands-on coding — writing, testing, and shipping production-quality code using test-driven development and continuous deployment practices. Throughout the day, you collaborate with product managers and other SDEs to shape technical direction and translate customer needs into scalable solutions. You also make time to review pull requests from teammates and mentor junior engineers on best practices. Some days involve investigating and resolving production issues, making quick decisions to mitigate risks and keep systems running reliably. By end of day, you have contributed meaningfully to services that touch millions of customer interactions worldwide. About the team The Associate Experience team develops products to support Amazon's Customer Service Associates (CSAs) in delivering seamless customer service. Our mission is to empower CSAs with intelligent solutions — powered by generative AI, machine learning, and automation — that anticipate customer needs and accelerate issue resolution at global scale. We build AI assistants, contact automation, and real-time insight tools that reduce CSA effort and improve the customer experience with every interaction. Our team values innovation, ownership, and collaboration, and you will have the opportunity to work alongside talented engineers who are passionate about using cutting-edge technology to make a meaningful impact on how millions of customers experience Amazon support. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience Experience programming with at least one software programming language PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

jobs.description: At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. ServiceNow Engineer About Lilly At Lilly, we unite caring with discovery to make life better for people around the world. We are a global healthcare leader headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana. Our employees around the world work to discover and bring life-changing medicines to those who need them, improve the understanding and management of disease, and give back to our communities through philanthropy and volunteerism. We give our best effort to our work, and we put people first. We're looking for people who are determined to make life better for people around the world. About the IT Organization Technology at Lilly builds and maintains capabilities using cutting edge technologies like most prominent tech companies. What differentiates Technology at Lilly is that we create new possibilities through tech to advance our purpose – creating medicines that make life better for people around the world, like data driven drug discovery and connected clinical trials. We hire the best technology professionals from a variety of backgrounds, so they can bring an assortment of knowledge, skills, and diverse thinking to deliver innovative solutions in every area of the enterprise. Digital Core is at the forefront of digitalization to enable and advance the entire company, with increased productivity and best-in-class Customer experiences. This team provides a robust and sustainable infrastructure of hardware, software and services that are critical to enable our global workforce. As leaders in technology, this team defines and leads the overall company technology strategy. About the Team Global Service Management (GSM) team works to enable Lilly to enhance global productivity and protect our Brand. The team manages the industry leading ServiceNow enterprise platform. We enable our 69k global workforce to accelerate how they work, manage critical action plans, and enhance their working methods/environment, and manage key vendor contracts / spending. In addition to maintaining operational excellence for our existing services, we must boldly innovate and enhance capabilities such as generative AI, automation & workflows across the enterprise. This will enable us to enhance our return on investment, improve user efficiency and experience, and help support the broader Company purpose of making life better for people around the world. What You'll Be Doing As a ServiceNow Engineer on the ServiceNow platform, you'll serve as a senior technical SME and strategic leader within our Global Service Management organization. You'll drive platform innovation, lead technical delivery, and ensure seamless integration across enterprise systems. You'll collaborate with architects, developers, vendors, and business stakeholders to shape and evolve our ServiceNow ecosystem. In this role, you will also be expected to leverage and contribute to ServiceNow's rapidly evolving Agentic AI capabilities. This includes working with the ServiceNow Agentic AI Suite — encompassing Now Assist (Otto), ServiceNow's generative AI assistant that powers intelligent search, summarization, and conversational experiences across the platform — as well as Now Assist for Creator, which accelerates development by enabling AI-assisted flow design, code generation, and natural-language-to-configuration capabilities. You will be expected to evaluate, adopt, and operationalize these AI-native features to drive automation, improve developer productivity, and enhance the end-user experience across the enterprise. This is a Dev-Ops role, which means the position operates on a rotational shift basis. You will be required to work either morning shifts or evening shifts to ensure round-the-clock platform support, incident response, and operational continuity across global time zones. How You Will Succeed Platform Leadership: Own the technical roadmap for ServiceNow capabilities, ensuring alignment with enterprise architecture and business goals. Solution Delivery: Lead end-to-end technical delivery for new features, including configuration, workflow design, UI customization, reporting, and integrations. Integration Strategy: Architect and implement integrations with LDAP/Active Directory, SSO (SAML, SiteMinder), REST/SOAP APIs, cloud platforms (AWS, VMware), and enterprise systems. Governance & Standards: Conduct impact analysis and code reviews to ensure conformance with architecture, data, and integration standards. Collaboration: Partner with Platform Architects, Technical Leads, and cross-functional teams to deliver scalable, high-quality solutions. Support & Optimization: Provide expert-level troubleshooting and performance tuning across the platform. Documentation & Enablement: Maintain comprehensive technical documentation and mentor junior engineers. Continuous Improvement: Stay current with ServiceNow releases and industry trends to drive platform evolution. What You Will Bring Deep technical expertise in the ServiceNow platform, including administration, scripting, and application development. Strong understanding of IT infrastructure, CMDB, and configuration management principles. Proven experience leading technical delivery across the full software lifecycle. Excellent communication skills with the ability to influence and collaborate across technical and non-technical teams. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with a proactive mindset and commitment to excellence. A passion for mentoring, learning, and driving cross-functional success. Basic Qualifications Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field. Experience: Minimum of 8 years of experience in ServiceNow development. Technical Skills: Proficiency in JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and ServiceNow scripting.Experience with REST/SOAP APIs and integration tools.Fluent in English for verbal and written communications, is essential. Additional Skills/Preferences ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA) certification is a plus. Applied knowledge of ITIL v3 or ITIL v4. Experience with AWS, VMware, JDBC/ODBC, and enterprise data management. Demonstrated ability to drive platform strategy and cross-functional alignment. A great sense of humor and passion for engaging people. Travel 0-10% Availability to work flexible work hours is/may be required. Your expertise will be pivotal in delivering platform capabilities that delight the engineers who depend on them, while driving tangible leverage and value across Deloitte’s AI engineering investments. You will leverage your engineering craftsmanship across platform engineering, distributed systems, and modern AI/ML and Data infrastructure, consistently demonstrating your strong track record in delivering high-quality, reusable, outcome-focused solutions. Key Responsibilities: Outcome-Driven Accountability: Embrace and drive a culture of accountability for engineering-leverage and adoption outcomes. Build platform capabilities that solve recurring problems once, well, for many teams—reducing per-team build and operate toil while ensuring consistency and compliance by default through high-quality, lean designs and implementations. Technical Leadership and Advocacy: Serve as the technical advocate for the platform as a product, ensuring capability integrity, feasibility, and alignment with the needs of the engineering teams who consume it. Participate in requirement discovery with consuming teams, component design of platform services, frameworks, and the AI control plane, and their development, testing, integration, and support. Engineering Craftsmanship: Maintain accountability for the integrity of the platform architecture and for the enterprise tech-stack conformance baseline that engineering teams build against. Manage platform dependencies, code design, implementation, the data and policy-as-code enforcement layers, and the OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation substrate—building capabilities that are operable, instrumented, performant, and drift-resistant by design, to the production standards set by SRE. Stay hands-on, self-driven, and continuously learn new approaches, languages, and frameworks. Create technical specifications, codify recurring patterns into reusable components and golden paths, and write high-quality, supportable, scalable code to ensure all platform KPIs (adoption, reliability-by-design, and developer experience) are met or exceeded. Demonstrate collaborative skills to work effectively with diverse teams. Customer-Centric Engineering: Develop lean platform capabilities through rapid, inexpensive experimentation to solve the real needs of consuming engineering teams. Engage with those teams before, during, and after delivery to ensure the right capability is delivered at the right time—and adopted, not shelved. Incremental and Iterative Delivery: Adopt a mindset that favors action and evidence over extensive planning. Utilize a leaning-forward approach to navigate complexity and uncertainty, delivering platform capabilities as lean, adoption-validated increments rather than big-bang builds, and keeping them supportable and maintainable. Cross-Functional Collaboration and Integration: Work collaboratively with empowered, cross-functional partners: engineering, SRE, security and risk, data governance, and engineering leadership and architecture. Integrate their constraints into the paved roads so that the secure, compliant, and reliable path is the easy path. Deliver capabilities that are admissible-by-design and submit them for admission, co-defining service-level objectives with SRE, who set production standards and own the admission decision. Learn to be a role model, leveraging these techniques to optimize platform solutioning and delivery. Demonstrate understanding of the full lifecycle of platform and product development, focusing on continuous improvement and learning. Domain Expertise: Quickly acquire domain knowledge of the enterprise data estate and the AI use-case patterns the platform must serve. Translate the needs of engineering teams, reference architectures, and governance requirements into reusable frameworks, the data platform, and governance-as-code enforcement. Be a valuable, flexible, and dedicated team member, supportive of teammates, and focused on quality and tech debt payoff. Inspire and influence teammates and product teams through well-structured arguments and trade-offs supported by evidence. Create coherent narratives that align technical solutions with business objectives. Engagement and Collaborative Co-Creation: Engage and collaborate with product engineering teams at all organizational levels, including customers as needed. Align diverse perspectives and drive consensus to create feasible solutions. jobs.title: Senior Technical Architect (DPO)
jobs.description: Job Summary Agentic QA Solution Architect Quality Solution Architect for AI Agents & Agentic Automation About the Role AI agents are non-deterministic: the same input can produce different outputs across runs. Testing them requires a fundamentally different discipline than scripted test automation - evaluation frameworks, scoring functions, and statistical judgment instead of exact-match assertions. As an Agentic QA Engineer, you will bring that discipline directly to our customers. This is a forward-deployed, customer-facing engineering role. You will work side by side with enterprise customers to design, build, test, and harden agentic workflows in their live environments - combining the hands-on coding of a software engineer, the quality mindset of a test automation expert, and the end-to-end design perspective of a solution architect. You will own the question every customer asks before putting an AI agent into production: "How do we know we can trust it?" Key Responsibilities What You Will Do Deploy and validate agentic solutions at customers. Work with enterprise customers to implement, integrate, and operationalize AI agents and agentic workflows in production environments - including APIs, data pipelines, and integration with existing customer systems. Design testing agents and evaluation strategies for deterministic and non-deterministic systems. Define what "quality" means for each agentic use case and turn it into measurable signals: evaluation suites, scoring functions, regression baselines, and pass/fail criteria that account for variability in agent behavior. Build and run evaluation frameworks. Implement automated evals (LLM-as-judge, semantic similarity, structured-output checks, human annotation rubrics) that track accuracy, latency, and cost across agent runs, and compare every release against baselines to catch regressions. Perform adversarial and safety testing. Probe agents for failure modes, hallucinations, prompt-injection vulnerabilities, and out-of-scope actions; validate guardrails, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and escalation paths before go-live. Automate the testing lifecycle. Build and maintain automated test suites for both deterministic components (integrations, workflows, UI) and agentic components, wired into CI/CD so quality gates run on every deployment. Act as a trusted technical advisor. Translate customer requirements into solution and test architecture; explain evaluation results, risks, and trade-offs to audiences ranging from QA engineers to non-technical executives. Architect for scale. Apply solution-architecture judgment to design quality strategies that span the full solution - agents, RPA/workflow/tools automation, integrations, and human-in-the-loop steps - and that customers can operate and extend themselves. Close the loop with product and engineering. Feed field findings - failure patterns, missing capabilities, evaluation gaps - back into the product roadmap and internal best practices, and contribute to reusable test assets and accelerators. Skill Requirements What You Bring (Required) Software engineering foundation. 7+ years of hands-on software development experience in Python, C#, VB.NET, or comparable languages, with the ability to write production-quality code and test harnesses. Testing and QA depth. 3+ years in software testing / test automation, including test strategy design, automated test frameworks, and CI/CD-integrated quality gates. Hands-on experience with AI agents. Practical experience building, deploying, or testing LLM-based agents and agentic workflows (e.g., tool/function calling, RAG, multi-step orchestration, frameworks such as LangChain/LangGraph or the Model Context Protocol), ideally in customer or production settings. LLM evaluation literacy. Working understanding of non-determinism, prompting, grounding, and hallucination, and experience setting up evals - including LLM-as-judge approaches, rubric-based scoring, and regression testing of model or prompt changes. Customer-facing experience. Proven track record in a forward-deployed, professional services, implementation, or consulting role: leading technical workshops, managing stakeholder expectations, and delivering under real-world constraints in customer environments. Solution architecture background. Experience designing end-to-end solutions across applications, APIs, and automation platforms - able to see the whole system, not just the component under test. Communication. Excellent written and verbal communication; comfortable presenting technical findings and quality risks to executive stakeholders. Fluent English. Must Have Skill UiPath Agentic AI Good to Have Skill Other Requirements What Sets You Apart (Preferred) Experience with agentic testing or AI-augmented QA platforms (e.g., UiPath Test Cloud / Test Manager, or comparable AI-powered testing tools) and with automation platforms more broadly (RPA, workflow orchestration). Experience with evaluation and observability tooling for LLM applications (e.g., LangSmith, Braintrust, Promptfoo, or custom pytest-based eval harnesses) and with tracing/monitoring agent behavior in production. Statistical literacy - able to distinguish signal from noise in non-deterministic outputs and reason about sample sizes, baselines, and confidence. Experience with test management and ALM tooling (e.g., ADO, Jira - Xray, TestRail, Test Manager) and requirements-to-test traceability. Knowledge of AI governance, safety, and compliance considerations for deploying agents in regulated industries. Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Willingness to travel to customer sites as needed. How Success Is Measured Customers move agentic use cases from pilot to production with documented, repeatable evaluation and test coverage. Evaluation suites catch regressions before customers do - measured by escaped-defect and eval-coverage trends. Customer stakeholders trust and understand the quality evidence behind every go-live decision. Field learnings are converted into reusable test assets, patterns, and product feedback.

Strong expertise in LLM evaluation methodologies, benchmarking frameworks, and model performance measurement. Experience implementing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), prompt engineering, and model fine-tuning solutions. Strong understanding of quantization techniques, mixed precision inference, calibration methodologies, weight packing, and numerical accuracy validation. Hands-on experience developing and optimizing SIMD-based kernels using ARM NEON, x86 AVX2, AVX-512, or SSE instruction sets. Experience with GPU acceleration technologies including CUDA, Metal, OpenCL, DirectML, or equivalent GPU compute frameworks. Strong understanding of GPU architectures, memory hierarchies, parallel computing concepts, and AI acceleration techniques. Experience with model deployment, inference runtimes, ONNX, model export workflows, and AI serving platforms. Proficiency with Linux development environments, Git, CMake, Ninja, compilers, linkers, shared libraries, and ABI compatibility. jobs.description: Company Overview Siemens EDA is a global technology leader in Electronic Design Automation software. Our software tools enable companies around the world to develop highly innovative electronic products faster and more cost-effectively. Our customers use our tools to push the boundaries of technology and physics to deliver better products in the increasingly complex world of chip, board, and system design. Position Overview We are seeking a talented and versatile AI / Machine Learning Engineer with 3–10 years of experience to design, build, and deploy production-grade AI-powered capabilities across our electronic design and verification tools. In this hands-on engineering role, you will contribute to the design and implementation of AI/ML pipelines and Agentic AI systems, bridge modern GenAI architectures with robust software engineering, and integrate intelligent capabilities directly into engineering workflows. Collaborating closely with domain experts, software architects, and product teams, you will translate cutting-edge AI concepts—such as intelligent copilots, multi-step reasoning agents, and automated EDA verification assistants—into reliable, scalable, and high-impact solutions. Key Responsibilities Design, implement, and deploy end-to-end AI/ML and Agentic AI solutions integrated into EDA software workflows and developer environments. Build and enhance intelligent agent systems capable of automated reasoning, planning, multi-step execution, and tool usage using modern frameworks (LangGraph, Model Context Protocol / MCP, etc.). Develop and optimize production Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines, leveraging vector databases, hybrid retrieval, metadata filtering, and semantic reranking. Build robust data preprocessing, feature extraction, model inference, and evaluation pipelines adhering to clean code, testability, and CI/CD practices. Work closely with domain experts (chip design, verification), product managers, and core software engineering teams to formulate AI use cases, prototype solutions rapidly, and harden them into production. Ensure robust model safety, evaluation against hallucinations, prompt injection defenses, IP protection, and compliance with enterprise security and governance standards. Qualifications 3 to 10 years of professional software engineering and AI/ML experience, with proven hands-on involvement in taking AI/ML or LLM-based solutions from concept to production. Strong proficiency in Python with solid fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, object-oriented design, modular architecture, and automated testing (pytest, CI/CD). Solid understanding of ML fundamentals, deep learning architectures (Transformers, CNNs/GNNs), feature engineering, data preprocessing, and model evaluation metrics. Practical experience building applications with foundational LLMs (OpenAI, Claude, LLaMA, etc.), prompt engineering best practices, and Agentic design patterns (ReAct, plan-and-execute, tool calling). Hands-on experience implementing RAG systems, embedding models, vector databases, and semantic retrieval strategies. Proficiency with modern ML and AI development libraries such as PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Scikit-learn, LangChain, or LangGraph. Familiarity with containerization (Docker), REST/gRPC API development (e.g., FastAPI), and model serving/evaluation workflows. Demonstrated ability to break down complex domain problems, rapidly prototype AI solutions, benchmark performance, and iterate toward production-quality implementations. Preferred & Good-to-Have Skills Hands-on experience with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT, LoRA, QLoRA), instruction tuning, dataset preparation/curation, or domain-specific model adaptation using Hugging Face TRL or Axolotl. Familiarity with graph databases (e.g., Neo4j, Apache AGE) and knowledge graph-augmented retrieval. Familiarity with C/C++, compiler concepts, or GPU profiling/acceleration (CUDA). Background or curiosity in digital logic design, SystemVerilog, hardware verification, or Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools. Hands-on experience with LLM evaluation frameworks (e.g., Ragas, TruLens, DeepEval) and experiment tracking platforms (MLflow, Weights & Biases). Why Us We are Siemens: At Siemens Software, flexibility is how we work—hybrid by default, built on trust and autonomy. Together, 30,000 people across more than 200 countries build technology that shapes the real world. You'll grow through real projects, strong technical peers, and global mobility, backed by the scale and benefits of an industrial software leader. We're committed to equality and inclusion, and we hire based on merit, skills, and impact. Bring your curiosity and creativity and help us shape tomorrow! Diversity & Inclusion We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome applications from all qualified candidates. Siemens Software. Transform the Everyday #LI-Hybrid #LI-EDA

jobs.description: Company Description It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started. Join us to put AI to work for people. Job Description Overview The AI Application Software Engineer designs, builds, ships, and operates applications whose core behavior is model-driven rather than explicitly authored — conversational and agentic experiences that interpret user intent, reason over context, invoke tools, and act on the user's behalf. In Field Service Management, this means building AI-native experiences for scheduling, dispatch, and service workflows that automate routine work, escalate exceptions, and improve customer outcomes. This is a hands-on, forward deployed role for a senior engineer whose first instinct is AI — someone who can shape ambiguous customer problems into precise specifications, author the instructions and prompts that govern agent behavior, build the application and integrations around them, and prove through automated evaluation that the result behaves correctly. This is not a machine learning or AI research role; you will not train foundation models. You own what ships, whether a human or an agent produced it. What You Get to Do Build AI-native applications. Design and ship applications built around agentic behavior across Field Service Management — scheduling, dispatch, and workflows that reason over context, automate routine work, and escalate exceptions. Work AI-first in delivery. Direct coding agents to build, refactor, and test; use AI to think more sharply in front of customers; and apply it as part of everyday engineering practice rather than as a side tool. Deliver forward deployed. Work embedded in customer environments, tuning instructions and evaluation sets on the ground, using AI to compress turnaround without cutting quality. Author and maintain agentic instructions. Write, structure, and version the system instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, and escalation rules that govern agent behavior — treating them as reviewed, regression-covered engineering artifacts. Build automated evaluation and test non-deterministic behavior. Design and operate golden datasets, multi-turn conversation suites, model-as-judge scoring, CI gates, drift detection, adversarial testing, and grounding checks that make change safe. Design conversational experiences. Build experiences that hold context, confirm before consequential actions, and hand off cleanly to humans. Collaborate across product, UX, and documentation. Bring the AI-first instinct into cross-functional partnerships, not just your own code. Own quality and safety in production. Monitor containment, hallucination, prompt injection, and data leakage, then feed failures back into specifications and evaluation sets. Qualifications Experience A demonstrated track record of building, shipping, and operating production software, including hands-on delivery of AI-native application features that real users depend on rather than demos. Direct experience authoring agentic instructions and prompts, designing AI-driven workflows, and building evaluation and testing for non-deterministic behavior is required. Experience with chat experiences is required; voice or multi-channel experience is strongly preferred. Willingness to work directly with customers in a forward deployed capacity is required; prior forward deployed experience is an advantage. Education Typically requires a minimum of 5 years of related experience with a Bachelor's degree; or 3 years and a Master's degree; or a PhD without experience; or equivalent work experience. Key competencies Software engineering fundamentals. Strong command of data structures, algorithms, system design, APIs, data modeling, and testing. Good to have technologies like HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Java. AI-native application development. Hands-on experience with agent orchestration at the application layer, tool and function calling, context assembly, grounding against enterprise data, and handling latency, cost, and failure. Agentic instruction and prompt engineering. Demonstrated skill with instructions, role definitions, tool descriptions, guardrails, structured outputs, grounding, citation, graceful failure, and disciplined iteration against measured outcomes. Specification precision. Ability to define a problem rigorously enough that another engineer or an AI agent implements it correctly, and to judge when to solve it in code, in instructions, or by delegating. Customer-facing delivery with AI-native speed. Comfort working directly with customers under real constraints, using AI to cut turnaround, and communicating capability and risk credibly to non-engineers. AI safety and data handling. Working knowledge of prompt injection, data leakage, over-broad tool access, and unsafe autonomous action, translated into concrete guardrails and least-privilege controls. Desired experience Forward deployed or customer-embedded delivery. Prior work as a forward deployed engineer, solution engineer, or in professional services, delivering software inside a customer's environment. A platform-level view. Experience with agent runtimes, context engineering, retrieval, and memory. Domain depth. Experience in Field Service Management, scheduling, or workforce management is valued but not required; the right engineer can learn the domain. Evaluation and observability tooling. Experience with evaluation frameworks, prompt and instruction management tooling, tracing for LLM applications, and analysis of production transcripts at scale. jobs.title: Staff, AI Product Manager
jobs.description: About the Role: GSK’s Enterprise AI team, a highly skilled applied AI group, translates the promise of AI into measurable impact across every major group at GSK — R&D, Medical, Commercial, Supply Chain, HR, Legal, Finance, and beyond. Bionic pods — AI product managers, forward deployed engineers, full-stack engineers, data engineers, and AI agents and workers — embed directly with scientific and business teams to build AI products that change outcomes. We are hiring a Staff, AI Product Manager to own the Orchestration and Automation platform tower: the low and medium code platforms where GSK builds agents and automations, and the enablement model that lets thousands of non-engineers use them safely. The estate spans workflow and agent builders such as Power Platform, Copilot Studio and n8n, alongside the adjacent orchestration tooling that sits with them. You will own the roadmap and the governance model, and act as the platform consultant business teams come to when they need to turn demand into working automations. Why This Role Exists GSK runs various low and medium code platforms, and demand from business teams outpaces any central delivery team. This role exists to take consolidation decisions, and to build the self-enablement layer — guardrails, templates, training, support — that lets citizen developers build safely without engineering review on every change. In this role you will be the person who: Owns the Orchestration and Automation platform tower and its roadmap. Takes consolidation decisions across the low and medium code platform estate. Acts as the platform consultant for business teams building on the estate. Owns the governance model that defines what a citizen developer may build unsupervised. How This Differs from Traditional Product Management This is not a traditional enterprise product role managing a source system’s roadmap, releases, and backlog. As an AI Product Manager in Enterprise AI, you: Build new AI products from ambiguous, unsolved business problems. Work with probabilistic systems, defining evaluations, acceptable error, and human oversight. Help lead a bionic pod, deciding which work goes to engineers and which to AI agents and workers, and how they hand off. Prototype hands on and are measured on business outcomes. Key Responsibilities Platform Portfolio & Consolidation Map capability against actual usage across the whole low and medium code estate, and recommend what consolidates, what stays, and what retires. Quantify value rigorously. Build credible business cases that survive finance and senior business unit scrutiny — cycle time saved, manual effort removed, licence cost avoided, automations running in production. Develop deep automation pattern recognition so you can spot the workflows worth automating and the ones that should be fixed at source instead. Strategic Prioritization & Portfolio Shaping Shape the platform roadmap. Maintain a living view of in-flight, queued, and de-prioritized platform work, with the rationale for each decision, and feed it into the broader AI Platforms & Tools portfolio. Make trade-off recommendations. When two business sponsors both want platform investment, define the success metrics, run the analysis, and recommend where effort goes. Protect engineering focus. Push back — with evidence — on opportunities that won’t move scalable outcomes. Engineering Partnership & Enablement Consult on platform fit and design. Advise business teams and delivery squads on which platform fits, how to structure the build, and what it takes to reach production. Translate ambiguous requests into crisp problem statements and success metrics. Shape engagements end-to-end. Define scope, success criteria, exit conditions, and scaling pathways before kick-off, then stay close as engineers execute. Surface re-use and platform leverage when a one-off solution should become a reusable capability. Design the human and agent split. Decide which tasks the pod’s AI agents and workers own, where engineers and business users stay in the loop, and how evaluation and oversight make that safe. Stakeholder Alignment & Communication Operate fluently with VP-level business and scientific leaders. Run conversations that turn fuzzy ambitions into concrete, fundable AI engagements. Build sponsor coalitions that secure data access, change-management commitment, and air cover for your engagements. Communicate impact clearly in language that connects AI work to patients, science, and enterprise outcomes. Measurement, Learning & Iteration Apply Enterprise AI’s value-realization framework to every engagement and platform in the tower, and improve it with what you learn. Run honest post-mortems and feed lessons back into how the tower selects platforms and prioritizes demand Required Skills: 16+ years of progressive experience in enterprise platform leadership, with a meaningful part of it spent owning a platform or platform estate end to end: roadmap, architecture direction, operations, and lifecycle. Demonstrated track record of taking a platform from fragmented or underused to well run: consolidation calls made, adoption grown, and the operating model that sustained it. Experience running a platform in a regulated enterprise, with working knowledge of at least one part of the pharma value chain and the data, decisions, and constraints inside it. Solid technical fluency in modern AI/ML, covering LLMs, agentic systems, AI agents and workers, data and evaluation patterns, sufficient to set architecture direction, challenge engineers, scope realistically, and avoid hype-driven choices. Experience leading engineers directly while also leading a far larger citizen developer community through influence, frameworks, and quality of thinking. A platform product heritage: roadmap shaping, lifecycle and version management, vendor and licensing ownership, service levels, and stakeholder alignment across a large and varied user base. Preferred skills : Deep, hands-on Microsoft Power Platform experience is mandatory: Power Apps, Power Automate and Dataverse at enterprise scale, including environment strategy, ALM, licensing, and the governance model around them. Has owned a low or medium code automation platform at enterprise scale and run a citizen developer or self-service programme covering thousands of users, with guardrails that held under pressure. Fluent with the wider low and medium code agent and workflow stacks that sit alongside Power Platform, such as Copilot Studio, n8n, and the equivalents from the major cloud vendors. Skills AI Platforms, Change Management, Data Analysis, Microsoft ALM, Microsoft Power Apps, Microsoft Power Automate, Microsoft Power Platform, Roadmap Development, Statistical Analysis, User Needs Analysis Why GSK? Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale. People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people. jobs.title: Engineer II, Data Engineer
jobs.description: About the Role: Enterprise AI (EAI) builds the data foundations that GSK's AI systems depend on. In our operating model, digital workers do the hands-on data engineering. They generate pipelines, test and deploy them, monitor them in production and remediate failures. Our engineers direct that work and own the quality of what ships. Humans and digital workers both rely on a governed context layer. It makes data, meaning, permissions and history retrievable at the moment they are needed, and sits above our data platforms and beneath every experience and agent built on them. The Data Engineer II independently owns a data domain. The role designs pipelines for complex use cases, owns the quality of what digital workers deliver in that domain, and keeps its context accurate and audit-ready. It also contributes reusable components to the platform and raises technical quality across the team. Why This Role Exists: Owns a data domain end-to-end, with clear accountability for the pipelines, models and datasets digital workers build and operate in it, and sound independent judgement on design choices. Makes digital workers more effective in that domain by improving the frameworks, tools and evaluations they use, so manual intervention falls measurably over time. Qualifications: 3+ years in software engineering with solid distributed-systems / data fundamentals. jobs.title: ServiceNow Senior Architect / Business Analyst
jobs.description: Who We Are At Kyndryl, we run and reimagine the mission-critical technology systems that drive advantage for the world’s leading businesses. We are at the heart of progress; with proven expertise and a continuous flow of AI-powered insight, enabling smarter decisions, faster innovation, and a lasting competitive edge. For our people—Kyndryls—that means doing purposeful work that powers human progress. Join us and experience a flexible, supportive environment where your well-being is prioritized and your potential can thrive. The Role Architects and Business Analysts are the key link between Kyndryl and our clients. You will work closely with business stakeholders, governance teams, project executives, and delivery teams to understand business challenges, define requirements, and translate them into scalable ServiceNow solutions. From project inception through successful delivery, you will help shape the vision, roadmap, and implementation strategy while ensuring outcomes are delivered on time and within budget. What you will do In this role, you will combine business consulting, process analysis, and technical leadership. You will facilitate workshops, gather and document business requirements, analyse current and future-state processes, and create functional and solution designs that align with client objectives. Acting as a trusted advisor, you will bridge the gap between business and technical teams, ensuring stakeholders clearly understand the value and capabilities of the ServiceNow platform. Collaborate with clients to understand business needs, challenges, and strategic objectives. Conduct discovery sessions, stakeholder workshops, and requirement-gathering activities. Translate business requirements into user stories, process flows, solution designs, and implementation roadmaps. Define and recommend ServiceNow best practices, platform capabilities, and automation opportunities. Lead solution design and architecture discussions while ensuring alignment with enterprise standards. Partner with development, testing, and delivery teams throughout the implementation lifecycle. Provide thought leadership on modules such as ITSM, ITOM, HRSD, HAM, SAM, SPM, CSM, and emerging ServiceNow capabilities including AI and automation. At Kyndryl, you will have the opportunity to work across diverse industries, clients, and cloud platforms while collaborating with global subject matter experts. You will continuously expand your expertise, influence strategic client decisions, and play a key role in delivering innovative ServiceNow solutions that drive measurable business value and exceptional client experiences. One of the benefits of Kyndryl is that we work with clients in a variety of industries, from banking to retail. Whether you want to broaden your knowledge base or narrow your scope and specialize in a specific sector, you can find your opportunity here. You’ll also get the chance to share your expertise by recommending modernization options, identifying new business opportunities, and cultivating relationships with other teams and stakeholders. Does the work get challenging at times? Yes! But you’ll collaborate with a diverse group of talented people and gain invaluable management and organizational skills, which will come in handy as you move forward in your career. Your Future at Kyndryl The career path ahead is full of exciting opportunities to grow and advance within the job family. jobs.title: Technical Instructional Designer
jobs.description: Hungry, Humble, Honest, with Heart. The Opportunity We are seeking a highly skilled Technical Content & Training Designer to join our Service Strategy & Enablement team. This role is responsible for creating high‑quality training materials, scalable digital learning experiences, and technical documentation that educate and enable our global support teams, partners, and customers. This position plays a critical role in developing content designed for both human and machine consumption—ensuring our knowledge assets are structured, discoverable, and optimized for efficient delivery across platforms. As a key contributor within our Global Support Organization, you will execute against an established content and enablement strategy, translating priorities into clear, effective technical and training assets. The primary focus of this role is designing, developing, and delivering high‑quality video‑based learning and enablement content that improves support agent readiness, accelerates issue resolution, and enhances the overall customer experience. This role blends hands‑on content creation with close cross‑functional collaboration, working alongside support teams, product experts, and customer experience partners to ensure content is accurate, relevant, and aligned with customer and business needs. About the Team The Service Strategy & Enablement Technical Training team at Nutanix is a globally distributed team dedicated to ensuring the Support organization is effectively onboarded and continuously enabled on Nutanix products and features. The team is instrumental in empowering support engineers to confidently support customers by delivering high‑quality, timely training and enablement content, This role reports to the Senior Manager, Service Strategy & Enablement – Technical Training. Collaboration is strongly encouraged, and while the team works closely together, individuals are trusted with a high degree of autonomy. The team is a highly productive, cohesive group where contributions are valued, ideas are shared openly, and every member is motivated to deliver their best work. If you are looking for a team‑oriented environment that values collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement, the Service Strategy & Enablement team at Nutanix may be an excellent fit. Key Responsibilities Content Development & Technical Writing Create clear, accurate, and user‑friendly technical documentation, videos, guides, and troubleshooting content. Develop digital training assets, including eLearning modules, instructional videos, job aids, quick reference guides, and knowledge base articles. Translate complex technical concepts into accessible, consumable learning materials for diverse audiences. Instructional Design Design and maintain scalable training curricula for support teams, partners, and internal stakeholders. Collaborate with subject matter experts (SMEs) to create scenario‑based learning and real‑world practice activities. Measure training effectiveness and continuously iterate content based on data, feedback, and performance insights. AI-Ready Knowledge Engineering Structure content to support ingestion into AI‑driven and self‑service platforms. Partner with AI and Knowledge Management teams to standardize content formats, metadata, and tagging. Ensure documentation aligns with evolving automation, self‑service, and intelligent support strategies. Collaboration & Stakeholder Alignment Work closely with Support, Product, Engineering, and Partner Enablement teams to ensure training materials are accurate, current, and aligned with product changes. Gather requirements, align on learning objectives, and manage the full content lifecycle from creation through maintenance. Participate in project planning and contribute to broader enablement initiatives. Required Qualifications 5+ years of experience in technical writing, instructional design, technical training, or content development within the technology or Support domain (8+ years preferred). Experience with AI tools for helping to create content. Proven ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, actionable, and engaging content for technical audiences. Strong experience designing and delivering digital learning assets, including eLearning modules, instructional videos, job aids, and knowledge base content. Hands-on experience with eLearning and video creation tools (e.g., Synthesia, Articulate Rise and Storyline 360), including video editing platforms with Generative AI capabilities. Expertise in documentation and collaboration tools such as Confluence, SharePoint, markdown editors, or similar platforms. Familiarity with learning management systems (LMS), learning content management systems (LCMS), and enterprise knowledge bases. Strong storytelling, scriptwriting, and instructional design skills, with an emphasis on simplifying technical material. Demonstrated ability to create accessible, globally scalable content (e.g., captions, subtitles, localization readiness). Strong organizational, and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage multiple initiatives and meet deadlines. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with a track record of effectively collaborating across cross‑functional teams. Attention to detail and a consistent focus on delivering high‑quality, well‑governed content. Ability to influence outcomes through collaboration and demonstrated results. Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Certifications in instructional design, video production, or related disciplines are a plus. Preferred Qualifications Experience designing content for support organizations or technical audiences. Working knowledge of customer support tools and analytics platforms (e.g., Salesforce Service Cloud, Confluence). Ability to structure content for AI ingestion, search optimization, and self‑service flows. Understanding of customer support workflows, troubleshooting processes, or SaaS environments. Experience with metadata, tagging standards, and content governance models. UX writing,graphic design, and animation experience is a plus. Work Arrangement Hybrid: This role operates in a hybrid capacity, blending the benefits of remote work with the advantages of in-person collaboration. For most roles, that will mean coming into an office a minimum of 3 days per week. Additional team-specific guidance and norms will be provided by your manager.

Software Engineering Managers have not only the technical expertise to take on and provide technical leadership to major projects, but also manage a team of Engineers. You not only optimize your own code but make sure Engineers are able to optimize theirs. As a Software Engineering Manager you manage your project goals, contribute to product strategy and help develop your team. Teams work all across the company, in areas such as information retrieval, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking, security, data compression, user interface design; the list goes on and is growing every day. jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description: Job ID 72346 Category Enterprise Technology Location Chennai, India Work Type On-site Who You Are An agent orchestrator, not a typist. You don't want to be a faster keyboard. You want to be a manager of agents — handing off the heavy lifting, reviewing the output, and keeping your hands on the architecture. The IDE is a cockpit for orchestration, not a text editor. Productively lazy. Your dream workflow: describe the requirement, let the agent build it, verify, ship, next. You automate anything a human shouldn't be doing twice. Your biggest bottleneck should be deciding what to build — while AI executes the how . Fundamentals first. Data structures, algorithms, distributed systems, networking — you understand the machine, not just the library that wraps it. When a framework breaks, you fix it. When AI gives you the wrong answer, you catch it. Orchestrating agents only works if you can tell good output from garbage. First-principles thinker with vision. You break problems to their core, question the assumptions, and rebuild. A software engineer's job is to architect solutions, not wrestle with syntax. You don't copy an architecture because "that's how it's done" — you ask why and decide if there's a better way. High agency. You don't wait for perfect specs or permission. You find a path, propose it, and move. Large organizations have walls; you figure out which ones to go through, around, or remove — and you do it constructively. Bias for action. Requirements will be messy and priorities will shift. You ship v1, learn, and iterate instead of living in design review. Why This Role Ford is a 120-year-old company moving fast on AI, and that's the real challenge: building world-class AI applications inside a large enterprise with real constraints — security, compliance, legacy systems. The engineers who thrive here treat those constraints as problems to solve, not reasons to stop. If you want a place where everything is already figured out, this isn't it. If you're a 10x thinker who wants to build something that matters — and have the grit to push through the hard parts — let's talk. What You'll Do Orchestrate agents to build. Use AI as your default way of working — agents do the heavy lifting, you direct, review, and harden. You set the bar for how the team builds with AI. Build the AI use cases. Design and ship AI-powered applications and agents — RAG pipelines, LLM integrations, agentic workflows. Understand what's happening under the hood and make it work in production, at scale. Ship cloud-native systems on GCP. Design, deploy, operate. You own the architecture, the infrastructure-as-code, and the CI/CD pipeline. No throwing code over the wall. Connect systems that don't want to be connected. Build the integration layer across enterprise SaaS platforms. Expect messy APIs, legacy constraints, and creative problem-solving. Automate what shouldn't be manual. If a human repeats it, you write the code — or point an agent at it — to stop it. Make other engineers faster. Build the tools, agent workflows, and guardrails that remove friction. Developer productivity is a multiplier. Requirements BS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. MS is a plus, not a substitute for shipping software. 2+ years building and deploying full-stack applications in production. 2+ years on cloud-native platforms (GCP preferred). Demonstrable experience building AI agents or applications — show us what you've built, not what you've read. What You Bring Python — deep. You write production systems, not just scripts. JavaScript / TypeScript — React, Node.js, or equivalent. A real frontend and a real API. Front-end strength is a big plus. AI engineering — LLMs, embeddings, vector stores, RAG. Comfortable building agents and evaluation pipelines. Bonus for fine-tuning or eval work. AI-assisted development — fluent with modern AI coding tools and agent workflows, and clear-eyed about where they help and where they don't. GCP — Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, GKE, BigQuery, Cloud Storage. Deployed and operated, not just tutorials. Databases — relational and NoSQL. You know when to use what, and why. APIs & microservices — designed and built RESTful services at scale. Git, IaC & CI/CD — Terraform, Cloud Build, or equivalent. Reproducible, version-controlled infrastructure and disciplined code review.

Strong planning and time management; ability to handle multiple assignments under deadlines with proactive risk and issue management. Collaborative and solution-focused approach; ability to challenge the status quo constructively. Practical prompt engineering to drive repeatable outputs (impact assessments, mapping rules, test scenarios, defect triage summaries, stakeholder narratives). Ability to review and validate artificial intelligence-generated outputs against source regulatory text, control rules, and expected results (human-in-the-loop). jobs.description: Date posted 10/29/2026 Category Engineering Hire Type Employee Job ID 19518 Remote Eligible No Date Posted 10/29/2026 Memory Layout, Staff Engineer We Are Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow. You Are You have spent years in the trenches of custom layout, and somewhere along the way you realized the real leverage is not in drawing one more SRAM cell, it is in building the frameworks that let hundreds of those cells get generated correctly, verified automatically, and scaled to the next node without reinventing everything. You think in systems, not schematics. When you look at a new process node, you are already mapping out the design rules, the automation gaps, and the verification bottlenecks before anyone asks. You are the engineer who gets called when a layout flow breaks at 3nm or when a compiler needs to scale and no one is sure how to get StarRC and Custom Compiler to play nicely together. You do not just script solutions, you architect them with an eye toward maintainability, reuse, and the next three nodes. You have strong opinions about what good automation looks like, and you are not afraid to push back when a methodology does not serve the people who will actually use it. At Synopsys, you will define how next-generation embedded memory gets built, not by drawing it yourself, but by creating the infrastructure that makes it possible for teams across the company to do it faster, cleaner, and more reliably. What You'll Be Doing Lead technology studies and process entitlement evaluations for advanced nodes (FinFET, GAA) to define what is physically possible and translate that into actionable layout guidelines for embedded memory compiler teams Architect and build layout automation frameworks using Python and TCL that generate, verify, and validate custom memory IP layouts at scale, not one-off scripts but production infrastructure Develop and maintain automated physical verification flows integrating Synopsys Custom Compiler, StarRC for parasitic extraction, and Ansys Totem for EM/IR reliability analysis across memory compiler products Author and document physical implementation design rules, best practices, and layout methodologies that become the standard for how SRAM, ROM, and register file compilers are built and scaled Evaluate next-generation EDA tools and capabilities, working directly with vendors and internal teams to define what gets adopted, how it gets integrated, and what productivity gains are realistic Provide technical leadership and mentorship to layout development teams, troubleshooting complex verification failures, flow bottlenecks, and tool integration issues that block progress Collaborate with foundry partners on design-technology co-optimization, feeding real-world layout constraints and automation needs back into process development discussions The Impact You Will Have Enable Synopsys memory compiler teams to scale to next-generation nodes faster by defining clear, automated methodologies that eliminate guesswork and rework Reduce time-to-market for embedded memory IP by building verification and extraction flows that catch issues early and run without manual intervention Improve layout productivity across the organization by delivering automation tools and infrastructure that teams actually use and trust Influence foundry roadmaps and EDA tool development by representing real custom layout challenges and methodology needs in co-optimization discussions Establish the technical standard for how advanced memory architectures are physically implemented, verified, and delivered at Synopsys Mentor and elevate layout engineers by providing them with better tools, clearer guidelines, and a methodology framework that scales with their work Drive reliability and quality improvements by automating EM/IR analysis and parasitic extraction in ways that surface problems before tapeout What You'll Need 8+ years of hands-on experience in custom IC layout methodology, EDA automation, or physical design enablement, with a strong focus on embedded memory architectures like SRAM, ROM, or register files Deep proficiency in Python and TCL for building production-grade layout automation tools, verification flows, and EDA infrastructure, not just scripting but software development Extensive experience developing and deploying automated physical verification flows using Synopsys Custom Compiler, StarRC, Ansys Totem, or equivalent industry-standard tools Solid understanding of advanced process nodes (FinFET, GAA, 5nm and below) and the ability to translate complex foundry design rules into engineering guidelines and automation requirements Strong working knowledge of DRC/LVS/Antenna checking, EM/IR drop analysis, and parasitic extraction methodologies in the context of full-custom layout Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Science, or related field with a focus on EDA or layout methodology Experience collaborating with foundry teams on design-technology co-optimization or familiarity with AI/ML frameworks for automating engineering tasks is a strong plus Who You Are You can walk into a room with a process design kit and walk out with a methodology roadmap that accounts for layout complexity, tool limitations, and team bandwidth When a verification flow fails in a way no one has seen before, you do not escalate immediately, you dig into the tool logs, reproduce the issue, and figure out what broke and why You write automation code that other engineers can actually read, maintain, and extend six months later without needing you to explain every function You have a point of view on what good layout methodology looks like and you are comfortable defending it in a room full of senior engineers who may not agree You can explain a complex tradeoff between layout density, verification runtime, and EM reliability to a product manager in two sentences without losing the technical nuance You stay current on EDA tool capabilities, process technology trends, and automation techniques because you know that what worked at 7nm will not necessarily work at 3nm The Team You'll Be Part Of You will join the Memory Layout Methodology and Automation team in Noida, a group responsible for defining how embedded memory compilers are physically implemented, verified, and scaled across Synopsys IP products. This is a technical leadership role where your work directly shapes the infrastructure and guidelines that memory development teams rely on to deliver next-generation SRAM, ROM, and register file IP to customers.
